strengths: Novel and insightful threat formulation: The paper introduces Erasure Evasion Backdoors (EEB), exposing an important vulnerability in diffusion model sanitization where pre-erasure backdoors survive post-hoc concept erasure.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The study benchmarks four backdoor instantiations across six distinct erasure methods (including state-of-the-art robust techniques like RECE, RECELER, and AdvUnlearn) on three different tasks (celebrity identities, CIFAR-10 objects, and I2P explicit content).

Principled methodology (EEBdeep): The proposed score-distillation approach across the diffusion pipeline demonstrates why parameter-wide interventions significantly out-persist surface-level or cross-attention-only perturbations against robust erasure algorithms.

Cross-architecture validation: The authors successfully validate that the vulnerability transfers beyond Stable Diffusion v1.4 to SD v2.1 and modern diffusion transformer architectures (FLUX.1 [dev]).

Thorough supplementary analysis: Provides detailed intermediate checkpoint trajectory tracking, ablation studies over loss components/hyperparameters, multi-trigger evaluations, and discussion on anomaly detection/activation monitoring.
weaknesses: Threat model applicability nuances: The attack assumes the adversary anticipates which exact concepts will be targeted for downstream erasure. While reasonable for common safety targets (e.g., explicit content, copyright-sensitive entities), its practicality against arbitrary ad-hoc unlearning requests could be discussed more comprehensively in relation to inference-time adversarial prompt attacks.

Variability against robust defenses: Performance against robust defenses such as RECELER and AdvUnlearn varies considerably depending on the attack locus (e.g., RECELER reduces EEBdeep ASR to 18.96% on celebrity erasure in Table 3). A more formal theoretical explanation of the representation geometry under which adversarial prompt searches fail to intersect the backdoor trigger manifold would enhance the paper.

Minor editing discrepancies: The text in the Supplementary Material (e.g., Section D overview on page 14 and runtimes discussion on page 21) refers to 'DISA' instead of 'EEBdeep', indicating leftover draft naming.

strengths: Novel and insightful threat model: Connecting backdoor vulnerabilities directly to concept erasure exposes an important blind spot in current generative AI safety and machine unlearning research.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The authors systematically evaluate four backdoor attack variants across six state-of-the-art erasure methods (including robust adversarial unlearning techniques like RECE, RECELER, and AdvUnlearn) on three diverse tasks (celebrity identity, object erasure, and explicit content removal).

Methodological breadth across access levels and architectures: The paper examines both black-box dirty-label data poisoning and white-box weight interventions (from text encoder to full U-Net LoRA distillation), and shows that the vulnerability transfers from U-Net models (SD v1.4, SD v2.1) to modern DiT models (FLUX.1 [dev]).

Thorough analytical insights and ablations: The trajectory analysis over erasure iterations (Figure 9) and the component ablations (Table 8, 9) clearly substantiate why deep parameter updates (EEBdeep) remain persistent even when standard erasure target accuracy drops to zero.

Dual utility as an evaluation benchmark: The paper constructively frames EEB not only as an attack vector, but as an adversarial stress-testing diagnostic tool to evaluate whether unlearning methods achieve true semantic concept removal rather than superficial prompt-space disconnection.
weaknesses: Real-world deployment assumptions: The threat model assumes that the entity applying concept erasure is downloading a third-party checkpoint or fine-tuning on poisoned web corpora prior to sanitization. In many enterprise settings, model developers train foundational checkpoints from scratch internally before unlearning, which somewhat restricts the real-world operational scenarios of the white-box variants.

Capacity limitations in multi-trigger scenarios: As demonstrated in Table 12, scaling EEBdeep to multiple simultaneous trigger-target pairs shows significant variance and degradation (with some concepts failing to implant entirely), indicating that capacity and interference across multiple backdoors remain unresolved.
Residual naming inconsistencies: There are minor draft artifacts in the supplementary text where the method is referred to as 'DISA' instead of 'EEBdeep' (e.g., Section D.3 and Section F).

Interaction with inference-time safeguards: While parameter erasure is successfully evaded, the paper does not investigate whether multi-modal inference guardrails or output safety classifiers (e.g., standard safety checkers) would catch the triggered unsafe generations.

strengths: Novel and insightful threat model: The paper identifies a timely and critical blind spot in concept erasure for text-to-image diffusion models, demonstrating that pre-erasure backdoors (Erasure Evasion Backdoors, EEB) can survive post-hoc sanitization even when defenses are explicitly designed for adversarial robustness.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The study benchmarks four attack variants (data poisoning, text encoder modification, cross-attention remapping, and full-pipeline score distillation) against six state-of-the-art erasure methods (ESD, UCE, MACE, RECE, RECELER, AdvUnlearn) across three realistic scenarios (celebrities, objects, and explicit content).

Cross-architecture generality: The paper convincingly demonstrates that this vulnerability is not restricted to SD v1.4, showing successful evasion on SD v2.1 and the modern flow-matching transformer FLUX.1 [dev].

Thorough ablation and diagnostic analyses: The trajectory analysis, multi-trigger evaluations, sensitivity studies on the loss weighting, and investigations into weight/activation detectability provide meaningful insights into why deeper interventions persist while shallow ones fail.
weaknesses: Threat model practicality: The setting assumes an adversary accurately anticipates which specific concepts a downstream entity will choose to erase. While plausible for standard safety concepts (nudity, prominent celebrities), the practical attacker-defender incentive structure could be discussed in greater depth.

Preliminary mitigation: Section 4.6 discusses existing backdoor detection techniques (e.g., WeightWatchers, T2IShield) and shows activation shifts, but does not propose or demonstrate an unlearning algorithm that successfully removes EEB without degrading general model utility.

Minor editorial inconsistency: In Section D.3 and Section F of the supplementary material, the attack is referred to as 'DISA' in several places (e.g., 'our DISA attack', 'potential to make DISA more efficient'), which appears to be an uncorrected legacy project acronym for EEBdeep.
